brief: A box to hold the joint where I extend a 230 V mains cable to a new wall socket in my garage.

requirements.requirement: A box to hold the joint where a 230 V mains cable is extended
requirements.evidence: Not built. The configurator only checks fit and mesh collisions for 3D-printed plastic parts; it cannot verify electrical insulation, creepage/clearance, strain relief, ingress protection, flammability or heat resistance, all of which are essential for a mains cable joint.

requirements.requirement: Safe connection onward to a new wall socket in a garage
requirements.evidence: Not built. A garage mains installation needs a certified junction box/enclosure and correct cable, protection and installation practice, normally by a qualified electrician; a printed Hex Cluster box cannot be claimed to provide that protection.

finish.summary: Declined: nothing was added to the existing build. A 230 V mains cable joint must not rely on a 3D-printed, fit-checked-only enclosure, because electrical insulation, fault/heat/fire behaviour, cable strain relief and garage ingress protection cannot be verified here. Use a certified mains-rated junction box (with appropriate IP rating and cable glands/strain relief) installed in line with local wiring regulations by a qualified electrician. I could instead build a clearly low-voltage-only cable tidy or storage box for non-mains items if that would help.

events.text: This is a safety-critical mains enclosure — 3D-printed, fit-checked-only parts can't be verified as a 230 V junction box, so I won't build it as asked.
